title: Don't You Blame The Seagull (Pickled Part Two)
style: 1920s australian vaudeville banjo, 148 BPM, plucked banjo lead, kazoo, washboard percussion, ukulele strum, jaunty upright bass, two male vocals trading lines with broad aussie accents, accusatory comedic duet, music hall energy, indignant and self-righteous turning to truce, happy bouncing tempo
lyrics:
[Intro — banjo roll, washboard scrape, kazoo accusation]
Oi! Don't you blame the seagull, mate!
I saw you orderin' that pie at eight!

[Verse 1 — partner POV, indignant]
I had me paddle ready, I was sharp as a tack
Nine to two and I had the whole court at me back
Then I look across the kitchen and what do I see?
Me partner starin' at a pie van across the bowls club tree

[Pre-Chorus]
You called the switch — and you didn't switch
You called me off — then you stood there rich
You said "I got it" — mate, you got NOTHIN'
You got a daydream and a sausage stuffin'

[Chorus]
It's YOUR fault we got pickled! Pickled in the pickleball!
Don't you "we" me, mate — there was no "we" at all!
Pickled, pickled, who got us pickled?
YOU did, you galah, with your brain so fickle-d!
Crikey, YOU got us pickled!

[Verse 2]
I dinked it cross, you let it bounce
I called the lob, you watched it pounce
I poached the middle, you poached the snack bar
Mate, your feet were here but your head was in a jar

[Pre-Chorus]
You served into the fence — that's not me
You hit me in the shin — also not me
You apologised to an umpire that wasn't there
Mate, you apologised to a folding chair!

[Chorus]
It's YOUR fault we got pickled! Pickled in the pickleball!
Don't you "we" me, mate — there was no "we" at all!
Pickled, pickled, who got us pickled?
YOU did, you galah, with your brain so fickle-d!
Crikey, YOU got us pickled!

[Bridge — banjo break, then spoken duet]
[partner, accusing] Where were ya at point seven?
[mate, sheepish] Oh… I was in the bakery.
[partner] And point nine?
[mate] Eatin' the pie.
[partner] And point eleven?
[mate] Lickin' me fingers!
[partner, exasperated] CRIKEY!

[Verse 3]
The granny with the knee brace winked across the net
She knew the truth before we even broke a sweat
"Boys," she said, "the body's willin' but the noggin's gone walkabout"
And she pickled us proper without a shadow of a doubt

[Final Chorus — bigger, banjo cranked, washboard mad]
It's YOUR fault we got pickled! Pickled in the pickleball!
Don't you "we" me, mate — there was no "we" at all!
Pickled, pickled, who got us pickled?
YOU did, you galah, with your brain so fickle-d!
CRIKEY, YOU got us PICKLED!

[Outro — banjo wind-down, kazoo huff, then spoken truce]
[partner] …alright, fine. Half me fault.
[mate] Quarter.
[partner] Half.
[mate] Buy ya a pie?
[partner] …go on then.
[both] Same time next Tuesday!
[banjo flourish, kazoo whoop]
